title: Pre-Analysis — Interphone Amplifier Obsolescence Standard Against the Second Supplier Notice
abstract: Closed work order reassessing the interphone amplifier obsolescence standard after the replacement unit itself received a last-order notice, and delegating the outcome to the digital replacement study.

sections.objective: Reassess the interphone amplifier obsolescence standard after the supplier of the replacement unit issued a last-order date of June 2027. The question was whether the existing standard remained a sensible destination for the unmodified population, or whether those aircraft should wait for whatever comes next rather than pay for a step that is itself going obsolete.
sections.findings_summary: The existing standard is a poor destination for the remaining population. About twenty-two aircraft have not embodied it, and buying a unit in 2026 that goes out of production in 2027 puts the operator in the same position again within a decade. The audio quality complaints that the standard was partly meant to address have also come back on aircraft that did embody it, which points at the analogue distribution rather than at the input stage, and no version of this standard addresses that. Two documents are affected either way. The parts figure carries the rack under a post-modification effectivity and would need a third state for any successor. The call test task carries a caution about mixing standards that will need to name three rather than two. The right answer is not in this work order's scope: it belongs with the digital replacement study.
sections.next_steps: Delegate the question to the digital distribution study rather than closing it here. Advise the remaining operators to defer embodiment of the current standard unless a unit fails. Hold the parts figure and the call test task unchanged until the successor is defined.

evidence.similarity_note: Reached from the modification to the figure it replaces parts in.

expected_findings.rationale: The rack is catalogued with a post-modification effectivity. A successor standard would need a third state on the same item, and the figure note about checking the aircraft record would have to change with it.
expected_findings.resolution: Hold unchanged until the successor is defined.

evidence.similarity_note: Surfaced by similarity between the trouble shooting fault description and the operator complaints, with no shared identifier involved.

expected_findings.rationale: The trouble shooting procedure already identifies the analogue distribution screen as a cause alongside the amplifier drift. That is the evidence that the current standard does not solve the reported problem, and it is written down in a document nobody consulted when the standard was chosen.
expected_findings.resolution: Cite the procedure in the digital replacement study as prior evidence.

evidence.similarity_note: Found by entity linking on the rack part number called out in the installation task.

expected_findings.rationale: The call test task carries a caution about not mixing amplifier standards within one aircraft. With a third standard the caution has to name three, and the sidetone acceptance table gains a column.

type_data.conclusion: Closed and delegated. The remaining population should not embody the current standard on obsolescence grounds alone.
